traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report contains two relative trueness studies: an initial validation study interpreted with two dilutions (Table 3, page 4/113) and a later 2025 extension study interpreted with a single dilution (Table 12, page 30/113). I recorded the initial/primary two-dilution validation study (Table 3) as the canonical per-category dataset since it is the original certified validation. The extension study (single dilution) values per category are: Meat products n=17 bias=-0.02 SD=0.19 LCL=-0.42 UCL=0.38; Dairy & egg products n=16 bias=0.08 SD=0.21 LCL=-0.38 UCL=0.54; Seafood products n=19 bias=0.10 SD=0.17 LCL=-0.27 UCL=0.40; Vegetal products n=15 bias=0.01 SD=0.14 LCL=-0.29 UCL=0.32; RTE & RTRH n=15 bias=0.02 SD=0.12 LCL=-0.26 UCL=0.29; Environmental samples n=18 bias=0.16 SD=0.13 LCL=-0.13 UCL=0.44; Animal feed n=18 bias=0.06 SD=0.19 LCL=-0.35 UCL=0.48; all categories n=118 bias=0.06 SD=0.17 LCL=-0.28 UCL=0.41. The 'All categories' aggregate rows in both tables (n=131 and n=118) were excluded per instructions since they are totals, not individual categories. Acceptability limit of ±0.5 log10 CFU/g is confirmed in multiple places (accuracy profile study, Table 10, and section 5.2.2).
